title: Harmonic Stack Synthesizer
description: Five harmonic amplitude sliders over a fixed 440 Hz fundamental, with instrument presets and a per-period marker showing that timbre changes while pitch does not.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Acoustics
Signals and Systems

learningObjectives: Examine how overtone mixture changes waveform shape
Predict which frequencies appear in the spectrum of a given mix
prerequisites: A sine wave has an amplitude and a frequency

controls.label: Show individual harmonics overlay
controls.purpose: Draw each component sine faintly under the sum

equations: y(t) = sum over n=1..5 of A_n * sin(2*pi*n*440*t)
assumptions: All harmonics are exactly in phase
Only the first five harmonics are modeled
The plot is normalized to its own peak so shape stays visible at any mix
limitations: Real instruments have inharmonic content, attack transients, and time-varying spectra; none of these are modeled

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with instrument presets for comparison
keyQuestions: Do the cycle markers move when you raise an overtone?
What distinguishes the clarinet mixture from the violin mixture?
commonMisconceptions: That adding overtones raises the pitch
That a different-sounding instrument is playing a different frequency
assessmentOpportunities: Explain what is the same and what differs between two waveforms of equal period but different shape
